scope: Observation only (hardware-acceptance V3, ADR-0003 R1). One Arm VM on one hypervisor. Not a decision on R1, not hardware evidence.

platform.hypervisor: VMware Fusion on a macOS host (Apple silicon)

runs.python: a user venv on the VM holding the main checkout (pip -e, Debian CPython 3.13.5)

raw_non_identifying./proc/cpuinfo: no line carries the word 'hypervisor' (the x86 flag does not exist on arm64)
raw_non_identifying.dmi product_name: a VMware model string (generic, matches /vmware/; not an individual identifier)
raw_non_identifying.kernel log: ACPI tables carry the VMware OEM id

reading: On this platform the two DMI sensors read observed and the x86-only cpu_hypervisor reads clear, as ADR-0003 R1 predicted. systemd-detect-virt also identifies VMware (on arm64 from DMI). Apple Virtualization and other hypervisors were not available and were not observed.
